'''Jindal Vijayanagar Airport''' {{airport codes|VDY|VOJV}}, also known as '''Vidyanagar Airport''', is a public [[airport]] serving [[Bellary]], [[Hampi]] and [[Hospet]] in [[Karnataka]], India. It is located between Vidyanagar Township and a [[steel mill]] owned by [[JSW Steel]] in [[Toranagallu]]. The airport was built by Jindal Vijayanagar Steel, which later changed its name to JSW Steel. It opened in 1997 and began handling commercial flights in December 2006.

==History==
[[Jindal Vijayanagar Steel]] built the airport next to its plant in [[Toranagallu]] for use by senior employees.<ref name="outlook">{{cite magazine |last=Dey |first=Sudipto |date=6–19 April 2008 |title=The Second Coming |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kjEEAAAAMBAJ |magazine=[[Outlook (Indian magazine)|Outlook Business]] |volume=3 |issue=8 |pages=58–61 |access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref> It began operations in 1997.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.rediff.com/amp/money/2007/feb/06airport.htm | title=Govt may allow airports on private land | work=Business Standard | date=2007-02-06 | accessdate=20 February 2024 | via=Rediff.com}}</ref> In 2004, the [[government of Karnataka]] announced that the airstrip would be upgraded to serve as the new commercial airport for [[Bellary]], which was {{convert|30|km|0}} away. [[Simplifly Deccan|Air Deccan]] planned to fly to the airfield. Bellary already had [[Bellary Airport|an airport]]; however, officials said its runway was not long enough and there was no room to extend it. The government also hoped that Jindal Vijayanagar Airport would attract tourists bound for [[Hampi]].<ref name="th704">{{cite news |date=16 July 2004 |title=Bellary flights to use Jindal airstrip |work=[[The Hindu]]}}</ref> In 2006, the company, now known as JSW Steel, constructed a terminal building at a cost of {{INRconvert|25|c}}.<ref name="outlook" /> Karnataka governor [[T. N. Chaturvedi]] inaugurated the airport in November 2006,<ref>{{cite news |date=3 November 2006 |title=Hampi gets air connectivity from Bangalore, Goa |url=http://www.oneindia.com/2006/11/03/hampi-gets-air-connectivity-from-bangalore-goa-1162620390.html |work=[[Oneindia]] |access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref> and Air Deccan launched flights to Bangalore and Goa the following month.<ref name="dec1">{{cite news |date=1 December 2006 |title=Jindal airport opened for commercial operations |url=http://www.oneindia.com/2006/12/01/jindal-vijaynagar-airport-opened-for-commercial-operations-1164982130.html |work=[[Oneindia]] |access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref>

==Facilities==
Jindal Vijayanagar Airport has one asphalt runway designated 13/31. It measures {{convert|1956|x|30|m}}.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://aim-india.aai.aero/eaip-v2-02-2024/index-en-GB.html | title=Aeronautical Information Publication for Jindal Vijayanagar Airport | work=Airports Authority of India | date=2024-01-11 | accessdate=3 February 2024}}</ref> The waiting area in the terminal seats 50 people.<ref name="outlook" />

==Airlines and destinations==
Between April 2023 and March 2024, the airport handled 43,140 passengers and had 1,228 aircraft movements.<ref name="AAI3">{{cite web|title=Annexure III – Passenger Data|url=https://www.aai.aero/sites/default/files/traffic-news/Mar2k24Annex3.pdf|website=aai.aero|access-date=23 April 2024}}</ref><ref name="AAI2">{{cite web|title=Annexure II – Aircraft Movement Data|url=https://www.aai.aero/sites/default/files/traffic-news/Mar2k24Annex2.pdf|website=aai.aero|access-date=23 April 2024}}</ref>
